os_version: Debian 13 (trixie), kernel 6.12.95+deb13-amd64, headless server — Xvfb 1280x800 (X11) + dbus-run-session, NO window manager

stack_detection.method: ldd shows libQt6Widgets/libQt6Gui; after launch the app appears on the AT-SPI bus with toolkit attribute 'Qt' — both checks precede extraction
stack_detection.signature: libQt6Gui.so.6 mapped + QT_LINUX_ACCESSIBILITY_ALWAYS_ON=1 exported; AT-SPI desktop lists 'FeatherPad' (toolkit Qt)

channel_setup: Same no-root Xvfb + dbus-run-session environment as the mousepad cell. Qt6's built-in AT-SPI bridge (in QtGui) activated with QT_LINUX_ACCESSIBILITY_ALWAYS_ON=1; on a real desktop the bridge activates whenever the a11y bus answers GetAddress, so the env var is the headless belt-and-braces, not a special permission. Input via xdotool (real X keystrokes/XTEST clicks).

t1_read_text.detail: Same typed sentence read back character-exact through the Text interface of the QPlainTextEdit's AT-SPI node. Strings, not glyphs.

t2_enumerate.detail: 167-node tree, 45 SHOWING lines with extents — richer than the GTK cell because Qt renders its menubar even without a WM: File/Edit/Options/Search/Help all carry real extents ([106,50,29,19] for File). Qt's AT-SPI tree for standard widgets is NOT thin: menus, scrollbars, statusbar, tab list all present with correct geometry. The thin-tree risk is real but lives in CUSTOM-PAINTED surfaces — see the qBittorrent cell.

t3_live_value.detail: PX-7Q4K-LINUX-ATSPI read back from the live buffer.

t4_living_screen.detail: Identical to GTK: 0 events in a 3 s idle window; 18 keystrokes → 18 object:text-changed:insert events (~21 B each). The Qt bridge emits the same event vocabulary as GTK's — one listener serves both toolkits, which is the point of AT-SPI as the cross-toolkit merge.

t5_blind_action.detail: Blind click on the 'File' menubar item purely from its channel extents (click at 120,59 via xdotool): the menu opens and the channel itself proves it — 12 menu items (New, Open, Recently Modified, ...) flip to STATE_SHOWING. Effect verified in-channel, no screenshot consulted.

t6_pictorial.detail: No pictorial region in this app (none in tree, none on screen — consistent). The custom-paint question is answered by the qBittorrent cell.

measurements.notes: 331 tokens vs 1365 for a screenshot (4.1x) on a standard-widgets window. Walk 158 ms for 167 nodes (per-node D-Bus round-trips, same caveat as GTK). The cross-toolkit result: the SAME pyatspi client code ran unmodified against GTK3 and Qt6 apps — roles, states, Text/EditableText interfaces, event types all identical. AT-SPI really is the OS-level merge layer on Linux; the router does not need per-toolkit adapters for standard widgets.

runtime_verification.method: Root-window screenshots alongside probes; menu-open verified both in-channel (SHOWING states) and on the captured frame.
runtime_verification.agreement: Full agreement. Menubar extents match the rendered menubar; the opened File menu's items appear at their published positions.

permissions_required: None beyond a session bus (QT_LINUX_ACCESSIBILITY_ALWAYS_ON=1 exported for headless activation)
